title: Poggatacut, Sachem of the Manhassets of Shelter Island
summary: Poggatacut was a Manhanset sachem associated with Shelter Island in the early contact period. Records and later histories connect him with Shelter Island, Gardiners Island, East Hampton, and Montauk, and preserve several spellings and related names, including Youghco, Yokee, Yovawan, and Pogaticut.
content:
Poggatacut was a Manhanset sachem associated with Shelter Island in the early contact period and connected in surviving records with Gardiners Island, East Hampton, and Montauk. The cited sources do not establish his birth date and disagree about whether he died in 1651 or early 1653.

The surviving record places Poggatacut in land transactions and leadership contexts connected with Gardiners Island, East Hampton, Shelter Island, and Montauk.12 Because these records were written through colonial legal systems, the biography is strongest when it stays close to the named documents and avoids adding family details beyond what sources support.1

Poggatacut's story helps show the relationships among Manhanset, Montaukett, and neighboring Native communities during a period when English and Dutch expansion pressed Indigenous leaders into recorded land negotiations.13

Evidence Limits

The history follows the cited deeds, treaty records, place-name studies, colonial accounts, public-history sources, and later local histories. It does not add details that those sources do not support.

References

  1. John A. Strong, The Algonquian Peoples of Long Island from Earliest Times to 1700.
  2. William Wallace Tooker, Indian Place-Names on Long Island.
  3. Long Island Historical Journal source discussion.
why_this_matters: Poggatacut keeps Manhanset leadership visible in Shelter Island history. His appearances in early records show Native diplomacy and land relationships before town histories narrowed the story to colonial settlement.
